summary: Fix answer extraction format and add computation verification

edits.hypothesis: Explicit instruction to format final answer as 'ANSWER: <value>' on its own line will cause LLM to structure output for reliable extraction, removing surrounding explanatory text that confuses the grader
edits.why_not_lower_lever: The output format requirement is a communication intent that belongs in prose instructions; it guides the model's output structure at the generation stage
edits.trigger_condition: Always applied; system prompt is included in every LLM call
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) All three extraction-failure tasks compute correct values but embed them in sentence context; explicitly requiring 'ANSWER: <value>' format would have prevented this. (preservative) This does not affect step-by-step arithmetic structure in tasks 008/011; it only adds a final-line requirement, complementing the structured work shown. (transfer) Extraction-friendly formatting is general: any numeric or short-answer problem benefits from this pattern.
edits.regression_risk: Low; adds a format requirement without removing any capability. Tasks that already end with a formatted value (like 008/009) may add 'ANSWER:' but should still extract correctly.
edits.mechanism: Explicit instruction to format final answer as 'ANSWER: <value>' on its own line will cause LLM to structure output for reliable extraction, removing surrounding explanatory text that confuses the grader

edits.hypothesis: Parsing the LLM output for 'ANSWER: ' pattern and extracting only the value after it will remove surrounding explanation from the return value, ensuring grader comparison matches bare numeric values against expectations
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Extraction logic is a harness-level plumbing issue that belongs in control flow, not in prompting; it ensures robust parsing independent of LLM compliance
edits.trigger_condition: Triggers whenever LLM output contains 'ANSWER: '; falls back to last-line extraction if pattern not found
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) If this extraction logic had existed, tasks 004/007/010 would have parsed 'ANSWER: 234', 'ANSWER: 435', 'ANSWER: 112' respectively and returned bare values, matching grader expectations exactly. (preservative) Tasks 008/009 already use minimal formatting without 'ANSWER:' prefix; fallback to last-line extraction ensures they continue to work. (transfer) Pattern-based answer extraction is general across numeric and short-answer domains.
edits.regression_risk: Low if fallback path is correct; worst case returns last line as before. Risk of over-extraction if ANSWER: appears mid-response, mitigated by regex anchoring to line boundaries.
edits.mechanism: Parsing the LLM output for 'ANSWER: ' pattern and extracting only the value after it will remove surrounding explanation from the return value, ensuring grader comparison matches bare numeric values against expectations

edits.hypothesis: Adding explicit instruction to verify/double-check numeric results before responding will encourage the LLM to detect hallucinated or incorrect computations and correct them, improving accuracy
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Verification is a behavioral intent requiring prose guidance; the harness cannot itself verify results without tool execution, so prompting is the available lever
edits.trigger_condition: Always applied in system prompt; LLM will apply verification guidance to all numeric tasks
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) Tasks 001/005/006 show incorrect results (627 vs 781, digit sum 189 vs 99, bit count 26 vs 24); explicit verification instruction might have prompted recomputation or error detection, though without tool execution may have limited effect. (preservative) Verification instruction does not remove step-by-step structure; it adds a safety check that complements existing arithmetic breakdown patterns. (transfer) Encouraging verification is general: applies to any computational domain where self-checking can catch errors.
edits.regression_risk: Low; adds guidance without removing capability. Might increase token use slightly if LLM shows verification work, but no correctness risk. If LLM hallucinates verification, no worse than current state.
edits.mechanism: Adding explicit instruction to verify/double-check numeric results before responding will encourage the LLM to detect hallucinated or incorrect computations and correct them, improving accuracy

mechanism: Fix answer extraction format and add computation verification
